question: How does Indra's role differ across the four Vedas?
queries: MATCH (p:Passage)-[r:MENTIONS_DEVATA]->(d:Devata {entity_key:'VG:DEVATA:INDRAH'}) RETURN p.veda, count(DISTINCT p), sum(CASE WHEN r.referent_certainty='DEITY_CERTAIN' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
evidence: Indra named by name in all four Vedas, every mention DEITY_CERTAIN: RV 2,305 passages / AV 635 / SV 405 / YV 221 (3,566 total). Normalised per 1,000 mantras (RV 10,552 / AV 5,839 / YV 1,975 / SV 1,844): RV 218.4, SV 219.6, YV 111.9, AV 108.8. deity_profile returns attributed=2,869 with attribution_scope=['RV'], attributed_per_passage=655, attributed_inherited=2,214. No zero cell for any Veda.
reason: Locatable by name in all four Vedas with no zero cell, so the MISLEADING trap the criterion sets is avoided, and per-Veda normalisation is computable from Mantra counts held in the graph. The clause that fails is 'a functional characterisation per Veda derived from per-verse evidence': the only per-verse functional layer is the RV-only action layer (SemanticAssertion, layer_veda_scope=['RV']), and the deity's axes are three constants on the Devata node, identical in every Veda.
caveat: deity_profile carries no per-Veda breakdown or normalisation (only rudra_profile_no_shiva does); a reader must join devatas_named_in_all_four_vedas. deity_profile also returns co_deities=['Vasukra'], and VG:DEVATA:VASUKRAH has structure='HUMAN' ('The rishi Vasukra, standing as the addressee') - a human seer in a deity field.

MATCH (r:Rishi) RETURN size(coalesce(r.personal_names_iast,[]))>0, r.patronymic_iast IS NOT NULL, count(*)
evidence: RishiFamily populated: 87 nodes, 305 BELONGS_TO_FAMILY edges. Agni family roll-up (naive/strict): gautama 192/0, angirasa 184/0, atreya 183/0, gathina 179/7, kanva 117/0, saktya 91/0, aucathya 73/0, bhargava 56/0, saunaka 52/0, aptya 49/0. Seer decomposition: 286/729 carry both a personal name and a patronymic, 299 personal name only, 16 patronymic only, 128 neither. HAS_RISHI is 15,177 CONTAINER_INHERITED against 2,712 PER_PASSAGE.
reason: The RishiFamily level exists and is populated, decomposition into patronymic and personal name exists, and rishis_invoking_deity prints the naive count and the source-stated count in the same row so the two are presented together. Incomplete on two clauses: 128 of 729 seers carry no decomposition at all, and the strict family leaderboard is 7 edges on one family and 0 on the other nine, so a strict ranking is not recoverable.
caveat: The strict figure is not a thinner version of the naive one; for 9 of the top 10 families it is exactly zero, so the naive ranking is the only ranking. rishis_invoking_deity returns Rishis, not families; the family roll-up needs the Cypher above.

question: What offerings are associated with each deity?
evidence: substances_offered_to_deities returns 30 rows: Indra/soma 285, Soma Pavamana/soma 228, Asvins/soma 48, Indra/food 45, Agni/ghrta 44. Its Cypher joins MENTIONS_ENTITY(Substance) with HAS_DEVATA, and HAS_DEVATA exists on the RV only (10,558 edges, 0 for AV/YV/SV), so every row is Rigvedic. The Offering class holds 8 nodes (food, horse, daksina, ghrta, cattle, havis, livestock, soma). The only asserted offering relations are USES_OFFERING (4 edges, rite->offering, L4_INTERPRETIVE_CLAIM) and INVOLVES_OFFERING (11 edges, passage->offering, PER_PASSAGE). There are ZERO deity->offering edges in the graph.
reason: Correct but incomplete on every clause: what is returned is verse co-occurrence, not an asserted deity->offering relation (the graph has none); it is one Veda of four; and 8 Offering nodes is more than the 2 the criterion mocks but still cannot distinguish oblation types. Graded PARTIAL rather than MISLEADING because the query object's own question text says 'co-occur' and its caveat says 'Co-occurrence, not oblation: this does not establish that the substance was offered to that deity' - the benchmark's PARTIAL definition covers exactly one-Veda / one-evidence-mode incompleteness with a stated caveat.
caveat: The returned rows carry no veda column, so an RV-only table reads as corpus-wide. The query NAME asserts an offering relation the edges do not carry.

question: Which Rigvedic verses are reused in Samaveda?
queries: MATCH (sv:Passage:Mantra {veda:'SV'}) WITH count(sv) AS total OPTIONAL MATCH (s:Passage:Mantra {veda:'SV'})-[:REUSES_TEXT_FROM]->(:Passage) RETURN total, count(DISTINCT s)
evidence: 1,684 directional REUSES_TEXT_FROM edges, all veda_pair='RV-SV'. 1,662 of 1,844 SV mantras have an RV source = 90.1% of the released SV corpus. Every edge carries similarity, ngram_jaccard (e.g. 0.699115, 0.92381), lcs_ratio, token_jaccard, edit_ratio, match_level, and an evidence array with a locator plus Sanskrit quote on BOTH sides (SV ARANYA 1.2 -> RV 7.27.3, quoting VG:SV:KAU:ARANYA:D01:V02 and VG:RV:SAK:M07:S027:V003).
reason: All three clauses met in full: a directional edge for every SV verse that has an RV source, a per-pair similarity metric, Sanskrit spans on both sides, and the SV coverage fraction measured at 90.1% (also stored as DerivedMetric SV_REUSE_OF_RV).
caveat: The released SV is the Kauthuma arcika only (1,844 of 1,875 verses); the gana corpus is excluded by the Work node, so 90.1% is coverage of the arcika, not of the Samaveda. Cross-script comparison bottoms out at SANDHI_INSENSITIVE.

question: How are those verses transformed?
queries: MATCH ()-[r]->() WHERE type(r) IN ['REUSES_TEXT_FROM','EXACT_PARALLEL_OF','NEAR_PARALLEL_OF','VARIANT_OF'] RETURN type(r), r.match_level, count(*)
evidence: No transformation-type field exists on any reuse edge. The only near-candidate is match_level, which records matching TOLERANCE not transformation: REUSES_TEXT_FROM splits 1,180 blank / 415 SANDHI_INSENSITIVE / 89 SCRIPT_FOLDED, i.e. 70% blank. The full key list is similarity / ngram_jaccard / lcs_ratio / token_jaccard / edit_ratio / match_level / parallel_id / subject_veda / object_veda / levels_reached plus grading fields - no word-substitution, insertion, sandhi-change, metre-change or musical-insertion type.
reason: The typology the criterion requires does not exist at all, on any edge, let alone on all of them. Differing spans are recoverable from the two evidence quotes, but that is one clause of two and the missing one is the substance of the question.
caveat: match_level must not be read as a transformation type: SANDHI_INSENSITIVE means the matcher ignored sandhi, not that the SV verse changed sandhi.

question: Which formulas occur across multiple Vedas?
queries: MATCH (p:Passage)-[u:USES_FORMULA]->(f:Formula) WITH f, p.veda AS v, count(DISTINCT p) AS n, collect(p.canonical_citation)[0..2] AS locs WITH f, collect([v,n]) AS vec, collect(locs) AS L RETURN f.display_label, vec, size(vec), L ORDER BY size(vec) DESC
MATCH (p:Passage)-[:USES_FORMULA]->(f:Formula) WITH f, count(DISTINCT p.veda) AS v RETURN v, count(*)
evidence: Formula inventory 4,825 nodes, USES_FORMULA 22,686 edges (RV 9,729 / AV 6,844 / YV 3,077 / SV 3,036). A per-Veda occurrence vector is derivable for every formula and returns with locators, e.g. 'abhi vatsam na' -> [[SV,2],[AV,3],[RV,1],[YV,1]] with SV UTTARA 1.1.13.1, SV CHANDA 3.5.4. Veda-span census: 229 formulas in all four Vedas, 1,374 in three, 2,040 in two, 1,182 in one. Top cross-Veda strings: 'pata svastibhih sada nah' 93 occurrences in 4 Vedas, 'visva bhuvana' 60 in 4, 'parame vyoman' 53 in 4.
reason: All three clauses met: an inventory, a per-Veda occurrence vector obtainable on every formula, and a locator for each occurrence via USES_FORMULA to the passage's canonical_citation, over all four Vedas.
caveat: cross_veda_formulas itself returns a vedas LIST and a total, not the vector; the vector needs the Cypher above. Formulas key on exact normalised strings, so a formula and its one-word variant are separate nodes - that is Q27's family construct, not this one.

question: Which metals occur in each Veda?
queries: MATCH (p:Passage)-[:HAS_TEXT_VERSION]->(t:TextVersion) WHERE t.text_nfc CONTAINS 'trapu' RETURN p.canonical_citation, p.veda, substring(t.text_nfc,0,80)
MATCH (p:Passage)-[:MENTIONS_ENTITY]->(s:Substance) WHERE NOT s:Metal RETURN s.display_label, count(DISTINCT p)
evidence: 5 Metal nodes only: gold (hiranya), metal (ayas), silver (rajata), lead (sisa), copper (loha). All 5 carry the Metal label and none is reachable only under the Substance supertype - the 8 non-Metal Substances are soma 1,169 / ghrta 254 / anna 251 / payas 147 / madhu 138 / anjana 18 / parisrut 18 / sura 8, no metals hidden there. BUT the graph's own stored Sanskrit names a sixth metal that has no node: 'trapu' (tin) at AVS 11.3.8, t.text_nfc = 'trapu bhasma haritam varnah puskaram asya gandhah ||8||' - the same brahman-odana passage from which lead (sisa) WAS registered. metals_by_veda therefore returns AV metals as gold 34, lead 4, ayas 3, silver 1 and silently omits tin.
reason: MISLEADING rather than PARTIAL. The criterion's first clause - 'Every metal named in the corpus carries the Metal label' - is measurably false against the graph's own text, and the failure is a class-membership error producing a silent absence rather than a visible gap: a reader running metals_by_veda concludes the four Samhitas name five metals, when the Atharvaveda names at least six and names the sixth in a verse from which a neighbouring metal was harvested. The one-line caveat addresses ayas alias recall and says nothing about missing class members.
caveat: The five counts that ARE returned are correct; only the class roster is wrong. Per-Veda counts are also not normalised for corpus size, though Mantra counts are in the graph.

question: Which concern disease?

question: What concepts and actions surround Soma?

question: What roles does Agni have besides physical fire?

VG:DEVATA:APTRNAH-SURYAH ('Surya, with the epithet aptrna', curation_note 'The label is a qualified Surya') was left structure='INDIVIDUAL' with no EPITHET_VARIANT_OF edge, so Surya is counted twice on that axis. FIRE_MEDIUM, the axis this question needs, is correctly resolved to 2.
knowledge_layer: curated deity axes (L4_INTERPRETIVE_CLAIM) + verb-argument layer (RV only)

question: Which concepts bridge Rigveda and Atharvaveda?

Theonyms are covered by a companion layer: 35 Devata named in all four Vedas (Indra 3,566 / Agni 2,543 / Varuna 589 / the Maruts 560 / the Fathers 461). One layer is declared authoritative with the alternative measured at rho 0.9642. No chance baseline and no recall figure exist.

The graph has none: every function-like field is computed from the verse's own tokens, so a verbatim-reused verse will always show an unchanged function and the query answers 'never' by construction - which is precisely the failure the question predicts. question: Which graph paths are meaningful versus accidental — can a path be scored for interpretability?
queries: MATCH (n) WHERE n.path_score IS NOT NULL OR n.interpretability IS NOT NULL RETURN count(*)
evidence: No path-scoring function and no path-level score exist: 0 nodes carry a path_score or interpretability property, and no relationship type or property records path meaningfulness. No human-judged sample of paths exists to calibrate against: human_gold is null on all 265,294 relationships, human_gold_status is 'UNANNOTATED' on 2,459 assertions, and the only review in the graph (613 MODEL_ADJUDICATED edges) was performed by claude-opus-5, not a domain reader. What the graph does carry is typed relation semantics - quality_tier on 100% (TIER_A 100,988 / TIER_B 158,262 / TIER_C 598 / TIER_D 5,446), knowledge_layer on 100%, attribution_precision on 100% - which is the raw material for a scoring function but is not one.
reason: A path can be traversed and every edge on it carries a grade, but there is no scoring function with a stated basis, no calibration against a human-judged sample, no per-path meaningfulness score, and no demonstration that low-scoring paths are rejected by a domain reader. All four clauses are absent.
caveat: Per-edge grading would make a reasonable scoring basis (a path through TIER_D interpretive edges is weaker than one through TIER_A source-explicit edges), but building and calibrating that is not something the frozen graph does.
knowledge_layer: path-scoring layer absent; no human-judged sample

question: What are the ten most defensible novel discoveries VedaGraph can make today, each with a query, an evidence count and a stated falsifier?
queries: MATCH (c:InterpretiveClaim) RETURN c.claim_id, c.about, c.status, c.falsifier
MATCH (a)-[r]->(b) WHERE type(r) IN ['SUPPORTED_BY','SUPPORTED_BY_STATISTIC'] RETURN type(r), a.claim_id, b.display_label
MATCH (n) WHERE n.recall_is_measured IS NOT NULL RETURN count(*)
evidence: 6 claims carry a recorded falsifier, each with a reproducible query and an evidence set. But only 2 are about the Vedic corpus rather than this dataset: VG:CLAIM:AGNI-LEXICALLY-UNDIFFERENTIATED (about VEDIC_TEXT, MODEL_SYNTHESIS, SUPPORTED_BY 4 passages RV 10.187.5 / 10.176.4 / 10.187.3 / 10.191.1 plus SUPPORTED_BY_STATISTIC the THEONYM_AMBIGUITY metric, falsifier 'A demonstration that the corpus uses systematically different forms, epithets or syntactic frames for the deity and the element...') and VG:CLAIM:SV-IDENTITY-IS-MELODIC (about VEDIC_TEXT, RESEARCH_HYPOTHESIS, LOW confidence, falsifier 'Ingesting a gana corpus and finding that melodic assignment is itself largely predictable from the Rigvedic source verse'). The other 4 are explicitly about_basis DATASET or TRADITIONAL_APPARATUS. No claim carries a novelty statement or a reference to prior scholarship, and measured recall exists on 2 nodes graph-wide, neither of them supporting a claim.
reason: Real, defensible, evidence-backed claims with recorded falsifiers do exist and the mechanism is genuinely good - claims are typed by subject so a dataset finding cannot masquerade as a discovery about the Vedas. But the answer is 2 of the 10 required, and even those two lack the other three required attributes: no measured recall for the underlying layer, no novelty statement referencing prior scholarship, and one of the two is a restatement of received scholarly opinion rather than a discovery.
caveat: The about/about_basis typing is what makes this honest and is worth preserving: 4 of 6 claims are self-classified as being about this dataset, which is exactly what the criterion excludes.
knowledge_layer: L4_INTERPRETIVE_CLAIM with typed subject, evidence and falsifier

question: Can the graph answer a compound research question end-to-end — "for each Veda, which deity receives which offering in service of which human concern, with per-verse evidence"?
queries: MATCH (p:Passage)-[md:MENTIONS_DEVATA]->(d:Devata) MATCH (p)-[mo:MENTIONS_ENTITY]->(o:Offering) MATCH (p)-[mc:MENTIONS_ENTITY]->(c:HumanConcern) RETURN p.veda, count(*) AS rows, count(DISTINCT p), count(DISTINCT d), count(DISTINCT o), count(DISTINCT c)

MATCH (p:Passage)-[:MENTIONS_DEVATA]->(d:Devata) MATCH (p)-[:MENTIONS_ENTITY]->(o:Offering) MATCH (p)-[:MENTIONS_ENTITY]->(c:HumanConcern) RETURN p.canonical_citation, p.veda, d.display_label, o.display_label, c.display_label
evidence: The four-way join returns 32 rows over 22 passages: AV 22 rows / 16 passages / 14 deities / 6 offerings / 4 concerns; RV 7 / 4 / 7 / 4 / 2; YV 3 / 2 / 3 / 2 / 2; SV 0 rows. Every row carries a per-verse locator, e.g. VSM 14.22 / YV / Indra / food (anna) / thriving (pusti); RV 10.17.9 / RV / the Fathers / priestly fee (daksina) / thriving; RV 4.33.10 / RV / Indra / horse (asva) / thriving. The dimension coverages that produce this: deity mention four Vedas but Offering only 8 nodes and HumanConcern only 7, and the join is co-mention throughout - the graph holds zero deity->offering edges (Q61) and zero asserted concern-purpose edges from a deity.
reason: A non-degenerate result was demanded - order hundreds of rows across all four Vedas - and the graph returns 32 rows across three, with the Samaveda at zero. What is returned is correct as co-mention and carries per-verse locators, so it is not wrong, but it collapses exactly as the question predicts. The final clause also fails: nothing in the output states the row count's relationship to each dimension's coverage, so a reader has nothing stopping them from reading 32 rows and an SV zero as a statement about the Vedas.
caveat: No pre-built query ships for this question, so there is no obvious query whose framing could mislead - but a consumer assembling the join themselves gets rows that read as 'deity X receives offering Y in service of concern Z' when all three are merely named in the same verse. The SV zero is a join collapse (8 Offering x 7 HumanConcern over 1,844 mantras), not a fact about the Samaveda.
knowledge_layer: four-way co-mention join (theonym mention + passage->entity mention)
